item.title: RTT: Ref. 5372, Ann. 2 - Development of new robotic platforms in uro-oncology with applications in telesurgery and teleproctoring (Univ. BOLOGNA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-10-26 23:59
Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Bologna
Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-14 Chirurgia plastica e ricostruttiva, chirurgia pediatrica e infantile e urologia

The project aims to evaluate the clinical implementation of next-generation robotic platforms in urological surgery, analyzing their technical performance, ergonomics, learning curve, and cost-effectiveness compared to the established standard. The study involves a prospective comparative evaluation of oncological outcomes (surgical margins, disease control) and functional outcomes (continence, sexual function, kidney preservation) in key procedures—radical prostatectomy, partial nephrectomy, radical cystectomy—along with an examination of the enabling potential of these systems, including remote teleoperation, telementoring, and the integration of intraoperative digital technologies. The researcher will be expected to conduct research activities focused on the development of innovative resin-based and ceramic materials, as well as on the definition of new digital techniques and workflows in restorative dentistry. In particular, the candidate will investigate adhesive materials, composite resins, resin cements, and ceramic materials, their interactions with dental substrates, and their clinical applications through both in vitro and in vivo research protocols. item.title: RTT: Ref. 5298 - Study on rare endocrine-metabolic diseases (Univ. BOLOGNA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-10-26 23:59
Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Forlì
Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-08 Endocrinologia, nefrologia e scienze dell'alimentazione e del benessere

Rare endocrine-metabolic diseases represent a heterogeneous group of disorders, predominantly of genetic origin, characterized by alterations in endocrine function and/or metabolism, constituting a major healthcare challenge. Their high clinical complexity, phenotypic variability, and frequent multisystemic presentation often make timely recognition difficult, leading to diagnostic and therapeutic delays. The project aims to contribute to the early identification of suggestive signs and symptoms, to the diagnostic framework through an integrated clinical, biochemical, and genetic approach, and to the definition of therapeutic strategies, while organizing long-term follow-up for patients.…
